title: autotune: batching/caching defaults, quantization profiles and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: This PR implements end-to-end autotune defaults for batching and KV-caching, adds curated quantization profiles for commonly used model families, and ships a first-pass unit-economics (uecon) toolkit (CLI + dashboard hooks) to make cost tradeoffs visible to SREs and product teams. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/caching heuristics and quant profiles per workload which is error-prone and time-consuming; automated sensible defaults plus compact tooling will reduce per-token costs and speed up rollouts (ENG-5123, ENG-4987). What changed: 1) runtime: new autotune config and controller that observes sequence length distributions and p95 latency to pick batch sizes and cache TTLs; 2) quant: profiles for Llama2/Redwood-curated variants with safe fallbacks and quality-preserving bitrates; 3) uecon tooling: CLI to simulate unit-econ for traffic mixes and a small dashboard in the Console to visualize token cost/latency by model/profile; 4) docs and examples: migration guide, opt-in rollout docs and a sample canary config. Testing: unit tests for controller logic, integration test on perf-canary harness, end-to-end smoke in CI. Rollout: default is opt-in per-deployment; ops can enable global default via feature flag. Checklist: - [x] runtime autotune controller implemented - [x] quant profiles added and validated against eval harness - [x] uecon CLI and dashboard hooks implemented - [x] tests and docs updated - [x] perf benchmarks added to repo/benchmark-lab. Notes: this is conservative by default (no automatic quality degradation); quant profiles include quality thresholds and automatic fallback to fp16 when thresholds are not met. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and canary gating.

discussion: Evan Zhang: Can we ensure the autotune controller respects per-customer overrides? Author reply: yes, controller checks deployment-level pins and will not override explicit user settings.

Diego Alvarez: What safety checks are in place to avoid quality regressions with quant? Author reply: quant profiles include eval thresholds; CI runs a small eval set and the controller will fallback to a higher-precision profile if thresholds fail.
Priya Menon: CI flake observed in the perf canary job on first run. Author reply: fixed test timing assumptions and added retry; subsequent runs passed.
Evan Zhang: Approving pending a small docs clarification about rollout flags. Author reply: docs updated per comment.
release_notes: Introduces autotune defaults for batching and caching, curated quantization profiles with safe fallbacks, and a unit-economics toolkit (CLI + Console dashboard hooks). Opt-in by default; see docs for rollout instructions.
notes: This PR is the first phase; follow-ups will add per-model offline autotuning and tighter integration with the Optimize recommendations engine.
